t:
(a) Section 309 of the Act is repealed.  
    (b) Part B of title II of the Act is amended by adding at the end thereof the following new section:


“annual report
“Sec. 233. Prior to April first of each year, the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare shall make an annual report to Congress. Such report shall contain an evaluation of the programs under section 231, the need for continuing such programs, and recommendations for improvement. The reports shall also contain progress reports on the vocational training study which will be conducted under the supervision of the Secretary during 1966 and 1967.”

fable.w: The section repeals a provision and requires a federal Secretary to report annually to Congress. The tempting reading is that a formal reporting requirement counts as participation, but Congress is inside the federal government, so nothing crosses the federal boundary. No outside party (states, the public, experts) is consulted or given a role in any federal decision.
fable.s: the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare shall make an annual report to Congress

qwen_block.w: This section requires the Secretary to submit an annual report to Congress. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to it is an internal government action, not participation by outside parties. The text does not require consultation with states, the public, or other non-federal entities before making the report or its recommendations.
qwen_block.s: the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare shall make an annual report to Congress.
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the report contains "recommendations for improvement," it implies some form of consultation or input from outside parties. However, the text only mandates that the Secretary *make* the report to Congress. It does not require the Secretary to consult with anyone outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or experts) before making the report or the recommendations contained within it. Congress is inside the federal government, so reporting to it is not participation.

opus.w: The section repeals a provision and requires the Secretary to send Congress an annual report with evaluations and recommendations. Reports to Congress stay inside the federal government. No state, expert, company or member of the public is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, rulemaking or right to sue. The report's procedural feel and its recommendations don't change that, because no outsider is brought into a federal decision.
opus.s: Prior to April first of each year, the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare shall make an annual report to Congress.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Secretary to submit an annual report to Congress. Congress is part of the federal government, so reporting to it is an internal government action, not participation with outside parties. The definition explicitly excludes reports to Congress as a form of participation.
qwen_chat.s: Prior to April first of each year, the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare shall make an annual report to Congress.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the report contains "recommendations for improvement," it implies some form of consultation or participation with outside parties to generate those recommendations. However, the text only mandates the *submission* of the report to Congress. It does not mandate any process of consulting with non-federal entities (like the public, states, or experts) to create the report. Congress is inside the federal government, so reporting to it is not participation.
